rv.q: Former Cirque du Soleil clown Daniel Passer directs with the sensibility of a ringmaster, keeping the production's many moving parts in perpetual, exuberant motion.
This show got me engaged and laughing at the right places. However, I left questioning whether modern-day audiences can really appreciate dated material, even with a masterful cast and director.

As a slice of comedy history, this production was fascinating. However, for many contemporary viewers, it might also seem somewhat dated. childish, and naïve (despite the anatomical and sexual topics).
